items.name: Diced chicken breast
items.preparation: Cooked (grilled or pan-seared), skinless, cut into roughly 1.5–2 cm cubes; a few pieces show browning

items.name: Cooking oil (implied by browning)
items.preparation: A thin coating left over from pan-searing; not clearly visible

scale_cues: Stainless steel mixing bowl about 25–28 cm across, seen from directly above. I used the olive size (each olive about 2–2.5 cm long, about 3.5 g pitted) to size the chicken cubes. The food covers a patch roughly 10 × 9 cm in the bottom of the bowl, in a single, partly overlapping layer.
assumptions: The white cubes are cooked chicken breast, not tofu or turkey, based on the fibrous texture and seared edges.
The olives are Kalamata and pitted, at about 3.5 g each, with about 11 olives visible.
Cooked chicken breast has about 165 kcal and 31 g protein per 100 g.
Kalamata olives have about 175 kcal and 1.2 g protein per 100 g.
No dressing is visible. A small amount of cooking oil is included because some pieces are browned.
No food is hidden under other pieces beyond a single layer.
